name: Text Input Field
description: An accessible text field built on the native input or textarea: a visible label, hint and error text tied to the field, required and optional fields marked in words, the right type and autocomplete for the data, and a character count that never cuts text off.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing fields win.

color.note: Examples on a white background; check the project's own colors against the same minimums.
color.border: #6b7280 (4.8:1; a field edge needs 3:1, and the common #d1d5db is only 1.5:1)
color.error: #b91c1c (6.5:1 as text and as a border)

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Add or fix a text field: a visible label, an optional hint, an error that's read with the field, required and optional marked in words, the right type, inputmode, and autocomplete for the data, and, where there's a length limit, a count that never cuts text off. Build on the project's field component when it has a suitable one; otherwise use the native <input> or <textarea> with a <label>. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Built on the project's field component, or the native <input> and <textarea> with a <label>
A visible label that is the accessible name; a placeholder is never the label or the only hint
Hint and error text connected with aria-describedby, and aria-invalid while there is an error
Required and optional fields marked in words, with the native required attribute
The type, inputmode, and autocomplete token that match the data; paste always allowed
A character count that lets people go over the limit and says by how much, instead of maxlength
Variants: search, password with a Show password toggle, multi-line, read-only, and an optional success state for checks people can't see
Field edges and focus indicators at 3:1, text at 4.5:1, and 16 px text on phones
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a text field component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Choose what the task needs: which variants (componentSpec.variants), and whether the field has a hint, a length limit, or a trailing button. Leave out the rest.
3. Wire the label, hint, and error as in frameworkPatterns.field: a <label for>, aria-describedby for the hint and the error, and aria-invalid only while there is an error.
4. Mark required and optional fields in words, and put the native required attribute on required ones (componentSpec.anatomy.slotNotes.label).
5. Set the type, inputmode, and autocomplete for the data (implementationDetails.typesAndAutocomplete). Never block paste.
6. For a length limit, add the count in frameworkPatterns.characterCount instead of maxlength.
7. Style the states with the project's tokens, meeting the contrast minimums (implementationDetails.appearance).
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, and a phone, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people enter text with a clear label and instructions, hear the same information a sighted person sees, and fix errors without losing what they typed.

anatomy.hierarchy: The label names the field. The hint and the error sit next to the input, and the input refers to both with aria-describedby. An optional count follows the input. A leading icon is decoration; a trailing button, such as Clear or Show password, is a separate control.

slotNotes.label: Visible text in a <label for> that names the field; a native label is enough, and aria-labelledby is only for names that come from elsewhere. Required and optional fields say so in words: when most fields are required, mark the optional ones "(optional)" and say so once at the top of the form ("All fields are required unless marked (optional)"). If the design uses an asterisk, explain it at the top of the form, and don't color it like an error. Required fields also get the native required attribute, which screen readers announce.
slotNotes.hint: Optional short help, such as the format or why the field is asked for, in text below the label or the field, and in aria-describedby. A placeholder disappears as soon as someone types, so it never holds the format or instructions; a placeholder that shows anything needed meets 4.5:1.
slotNotes.input: The native <input> with the type that matches the data, or <textarea> for more than one line.
slotNotes.error: An element that is empty and hidden until there is an error, always in aria-describedby after the hint. It is never a live region: when errors are announced and where focus goes is the form's job.
slotNotes.count: Optional, for fields with a length limit; see frameworkPatterns.characterCount.
slotNotes.trailingButton: Optional <button type="button"> with an accessible name, such as Clear or Show password, at least 24 by 24 px (44 px suggested on touch).

value.description: The text. Controlled or uncontrolled, the way the project's other fields work. Never cleared because it's wrong.

error.description: The error message, or empty when there is none. Set by the form's validation (see the Form Validation Pattern) or the server.

required.description: Whether the field must be filled in; sets the native required attribute.

readonly.description: Shown and sent with the form, focusable and selectable, but not editable.

disabled.description: Not focusable and not sent with the form. Only for fields that really can't be used yet; say why in text.

success.description: Optional: a confirmation for a check the person can't see, such as "Username available", shown in text. Not a green border on every valid field.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Errors don't appear while someone types in a field that has none yet; once a field shows an error, the form checks it on every input, so the error goes as soon as it's fixed (Form Validation Pattern).
The error element keeps its place in aria-describedby; with no error it is empty and hidden, so it adds nothing (frameworkPatterns.field).

The button's name stays "Show password", aria-pressed gives its state, and focus stays on the button. The password is hidden again when the form is sent (see the Login & Registration Forms guide for the full pattern).

interactions.when: a search field with a custom Clear button
interactions.accessibilityNotes: The button is named "Clear search". Chromium and WebKit draw their own clear button in search fields, so hide theirs (::-webkit-search-cancel-button) when the design has its own.
No field adds its own Escape-to-clear: it would lose typing, and inside a dialog Escape closes the dialog. In a search field, Chromium and Firefox clear it on Escape themselves.

responsiveBehavior.layout: A field fills its container and has no breakpoints of its own.
responsiveBehavior.phones: Text is at least 16 px: iOS Safari zooms the page when a smaller field gets focus. Trailing buttons are at least 44 by 44 px on touch (suggested).
responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide and at 200% text size, labels, hints, and errors wrap; nothing is cut off.

variants.text: type="text" for names and other free text.
variants.email: type="email" with autocomplete="email" (or "username" when it identifies an account).
variants.search: type="search", named "Search" by a visible or visually hidden label. Browsers handle Escape and draw their own clear button (componentSpec.interactions).
variants.password: type="password" with autocomplete="current-password" or "new-password", spellcheck="false", paste allowed, and an optional Show password toggle (componentSpec.interactions).
variants.numberLike: Codes, card numbers, and IDs: type="text" with inputmode="numeric" (and autocomplete="one-time-code" for one-time codes). type="number" is for quantities.
variants.multiLine: <textarea> with the same label, hint, and error; it can grow with its content (field-sizing: content where supported).
variants.readonly: readonly keeps the value focusable, selectable, and sent with the form; disabled doesn't.
variants.withCount: A length limit with a count (frameworkPatterns.characterCount).
variants.success: Optional, only for checks the person can't see, with text such as "Username available".

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, state changes are instant.

requirements.1.3.1: The label is a <label for>, and the hint and the error are connected with aria-describedby.
requirements.1.3.5: Fields that ask for the person's own data have the matching autocomplete token.
requirements.1.4.3: Label, value, hint, error, and any placeholder text meet 4.5:1.
requirements.1.4.10: At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways or gets cut off.
requirements.1.4.11: The field's edge and the focus indicator meet 3:1 against what's around them.
requirements.2.4.7: Focus is visible on the field and on trailing buttons.
requirements.2.5.8: Trailing buttons are at least 24 by 24 px.
requirements.3.3.1: Errors are shown in text next to the field.
requirements.3.3.2: Every field has a visible label, and required and optional fields say so in words.
requirements.3.3.3: Errors say how to fix the problem.
requirements.3.3.8: Paste and autofill always work, so password managers and copied codes can be used.
requirements.4.1.2: The field has its name from the label, its required state from the required attribute, and aria-invalid while it has an error.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Tab reaches the field, then any trailing button.
keyboardNavigation.enter: In a single-line field inside a form, Enter submits the form, as usual.

input.aria-describedby: The ids of the hint and the error, in that order.
input.aria-invalid: "true" while there is an error; removed otherwise.
input.required: The native attribute on required fields.

trailingButton.name: Visible text or aria-label that includes any visible text, such as "Clear search".
trailingButton.aria-pressed: On a Show password toggle, which keeps the name "Show password".

screenReader.onFocus: The label, "required" when required, the value, then the hint, and the error when there is one.
screenReader.errors: Field errors aren't live regions; the form decides what is announced (Form Validation Pattern).
screenReader.count: The count is announced once typing pauses, through one status region (frameworkPatterns.characterCount).

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

field.description: A required email field and an optional phone field, with hints and an error that is empty and hidden until it's needed, and a function that shows or clears the error.
field.html:
All fields are required unless marked (optional).

We'll send your receipt here.

Include the country code, for example +44 20 7946 0958.

characterCount.description: A character count that lets people go over the limit, so a paste is never cut short, says by how much, and is announced once typing pauses. It also counts the text the page starts with, and the text a form reset puts back.
characterCount.html: You can enter up to 200 characters

implementationDetails.typesAndAutocomplete: Use the type that matches the data (email, tel, url, search, password): it brings the right phone keyboard, and email and url a format check. Codes, card numbers, and IDs are type="text" with inputmode="numeric"; type="number" is for quantities. Fields that ask for the person's own data get the matching autocomplete token, such as name, email, tel, street-address, postal-code, or bday; passwords get current-password at sign-in and new-password when one is created. Never block paste.
implementationDetails.lengthLimits: Don't use maxlength for a limit people can reach: it cuts longer typed or pasted text without a word (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit) and stops typing without saying why. Show the limit up front, count as people type, let them go over, and make the field invalid until it's shortened (frameworkPatterns.characterCount). Count characters the way the server does; the snippet counts code points, so an emoji counts as one. The count and the validity also cover the text the page starts with, such as a saved bio, and the text a form reset puts back, which comes back without an input event and without clearing custom validity; neither is announced. The snippet updates after the reset event has finished, and only if no listener cancelled the reset. After setting the text from script, run the same update. The server checks the limit again.
implementationDetails.appearance: States: default, hover, focus, error, read-only, disabled, and an optional success. The field's edge has 3:1 contrast against the background in every state, and so does the focus indicator: #6b7280 on white is 4.8:1, while the common #d1d5db is 1.5:1. The error state changes more than the color: it has its message, and an icon if the design uses one. Focus shows with :focus-visible, an outline or a ring, and is never removed without a replacement.

edgeCases.longText: Long labels, hints, and errors wrap; nothing is cut off at 200% text size or 320 px wide.
edgeCases.hintAndError: Both stay visible, and both stay in aria-describedby, the hint first.
edgeCases.serverErrors: An error from the server shows in the same error element, set the same way, at the field it belongs to.
edgeCases.prefilled: A saved value being edited behaves like a typed one, its count and validity included.
edgeCases.formReset: A form reset puts the starting text back without an input event, so anything computed from the text, such as the count and its validity, is updated after the reset event has finished, unless a listener cancelled the reset.
edgeCases.autofill: Autofilled values count as typed; the field's edge and text stay readable in the browser's autofill style (:autofill).
edgeCases.rightToLeft: Icons and trailing buttons use logical properties, such as padding-inline-start, so they mirror in right-to-left languages.

must: Build on the project's field component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
Give every field a visible label, and connect its hint and error with aria-describedby
Mark required and optional fields in words
Keep everything people type or paste
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a form or input-mask library, without asking
Use a placeholder as the label or the only hint
Make field errors live regions, or color an asterisk like an error
Use maxlength for a limit people can reach, or type="number" for codes and card numbers
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Every field has a visible label that is its accessible name, and no placeholder stands in for a label or a hint
Required and optional fields say so in words, and required fields have the required attribute
A screen reader reads the hint with the field, and the error too when there is one, with the field marked invalid
Errors say how to fix the problem, keep what was typed, and aren't live regions
Fields that ask for the person's own data have the matching autocomplete token, and paste works in every field
Codes and card numbers use inputmode="numeric", not type="number"
A field with a length limit keeps everything typed or pasted, says how many characters are too many, and announces the count only when typing pauses
The count and the validity are right for text the page starts with, and after a form reset; a cancelled reset changes nothing
Escape clears no field except a search field, where the browser does it
A Show password button keeps its name and focus, shows its state with aria-pressed, and the password is hidden again when the form is sent
Field edges and the focus indicator have at least 3:1 contrast and text 4.5:1, in every state
Text is at least 16 px on phones, and nothing is cut off at 320 px wide or at 200% text size
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, like its other form controls
